subject: Hosted API: geo data tenure, backups, and erase timeline (Acme Logistics)
messages:

Subject: Questions: Hosted API geo residency, retention & deletion (Acme Logistics)

Hi Sean,

I'm Nina from DataBank's security team — we run procurement for Acme Logistics. We have a short security questionnaire focused on where customer data lives, how long it is retained, and what happens when a tenant requests deletion. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's Hosted API?

1) Primary and backup region map for customer data associated with Acme's account (logical + physical location).
2) Retention windows for: (a) request/response payloads, (b) streaming session state, and (c) KV/cache artifacts (if any).
3) Timeline for a customer-initiated full-tenant erase: how long till tokens, metadata, and backups are purged? Any caveats (snapshots, backups, logs)?
4) Evidence: a policy or short diagram and an example deletion audit log entry (redacted) would be helpful.

We need answers by end of week to keep the procurement timeline intact. If file attachments make this easier, please attach stub copies of the policy or diagrams.

Thanks,
Nina Park
Security Analyst, DataBank
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@databank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Sep 2029 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: Hosted API geo residency, retention & deletion (Acme Logistics)

Hi Nina — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and attached: retention_policy_2029.pdf (policy summary) and dataflow_kvcache_v2.png (architecture diagram). I copied Marissa from Security/Compliance for any legal evidence needs.

Quick summary:
- Primary region: us-west-2 (customer data processed and cached here by default).
- Backup/replication region: us-east-1 (cold replicas for disaster recovery only; residency controls keep replication within chosen geography unless customer approves cross-region).
- Retention windows:
  • request/response payloads: default 30 days; configurable per-tenant down to 24 hours for hosted API customers on enterprise plan.
  • streaming session state (short-lived): up to 2 hours by default; session tokens and transient KV caches are ephemeral and evicted on inactivity, typically within minutes, but may persist short-term for active sessions (see attached diagram).
  • KV/cache artifacts: not persisted long-term for hosted API by default; ephemeral caches can persist up to 7 days if customer enables performance mode.
- Erase timeline: for a full-tenant erase request we start immediate deletion workflows: primary deletion completes within 48 hours for active indexes and tokenized logs; final purge from backup snapshots and long-term archives completes within 30 days. Audit trail entries are generated at each step.

Notes & caveats:
- Backups: automated daily snapshots are retained for up to 30 days; we do not store customer payloads in long-term cold storage unless contractually required.
- Logs: operational logs that contain metadata are retained 90 days by default; we can scope and shorten log retention under contract.
- Legal holds & subpoenas: deletion may be paused if a lawful hold is in place; we surface that to customers.
- Evidence: attached PDF has a short playbook and the diagram shows which artifacts are geo-replicated. Also included is a stub erase_workflow.md with an example audit line (redacted).

If you want, Ben (cc'd on subsequent messages) can give more detail on the KV caching and how we zero-out ephemeral storage.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@databank.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Sep 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: Hosted API geo residency, retention & deletion (Acme Logistics)

Hi Nina — Ben here from Platform Ops. A few technical clarifications to seed your reviewers and to address the three bullets: 

- Snapshots: daily snapshots capture the persistence layer's object state (indices + tokenized artefacts) but do not include raw request/response payloads unless the customer has enabled request archiving. By default we store payloads in the hot region only and they are excluded from snapshot exports.
- Acceleration: we can offer a contractual accelerate-purge SLA to 7 days for both snapshots and backups. That requires a reserved-capacity agreement or enterprise addendum; we can include that in the SOW for HS-78945.
- Sample audit line (redacted):

  2029-09-26T16:42:09Z | tenant_id=HS-78945 | action=tenant_delete_request | actor=acme_admin@acmelog.com | status=initiated
  2029-09-26T16:43:12Z | tenant_id=HS-78945 | action=tenant_delete_processing | component=ingest-cleaner | status=in_progress
  2029-09-26T16:49:55Z | tenant_id=HS-78945 | action=tenant_delete_complete | component=backup-cleaner | status=completed

We zero out KV cache entries by overwriting with randomized metadata and then removing pointers; ephemeral caches have independent garbage collection. The attached erase_workflow.md contains that step-by-step.

If you need cryptographic proof of deletion (e.g., signed attestations), Marissa can advise on how we produce those artefacts for enterprise customers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
